title: Wolff-Parkinson-White pre-excitation
summary: An accessory pathway lets the impulse reach the ventricle early, bypassing the AV node delay.

events.label: Sinus node
events.caption: A normal sinus beat begins. This heart has an accessory pathway, a strand of muscle across the left AV groove that bypasses the AV node.

events.label: AV node
events.caption: The impulse reaches the AV node and begins its slow passage.
events.ecg: The P wave is still being written.

events.label: Accessory pathway
events.caption: The impulse also reaches the accessory pathway, which conducts quickly and without delay. The adjacent ventricular wall is activated early: pre-excitation.
events.ecg: The PR interval is short and the QRS begins with a slurred upstroke, the delta wave.

events.label: AV node route arrives
events.caption: The impulse that took the normal route now emerges from the His bundle and joins the early activation, so the ventricles are activated partly by each route.
events.ecg: The QRS is wider than normal because the two wavefronts fuse.

events.label: Fusion complete
events.caption: Ventricular activation finishes later than the first pre-excited site, giving a wide QRS.
events.ecg: A wide QRS with a delta wave, followed by repolarisation changes.

teaching_points: Pre-excitation: an accessory pathway activates part of the ventricle early (short PR, delta wave, wide QRS) (slide 61).
The accessory pathway conducts without the AV node delay and can carry the impulse in either direction.
Pre-excited atrial fibrillation can conduct very fast over the pathway and is dangerous (slides 85-87).
